ROW BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 1 row):
  array.t 126 `arylen_p magic does not stop isa magic from being copied`
  -- perl-tests/array.t:466, `::is eval { pling peen }, 'pling', ...`

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    package Peen; sub pling { 'pling' }
    package peen; sub pling { 'pling-lc' }
    package main;
    print "Upper=[", (eval { pling Peen } // "ERR:$@"), "]\n";
    print "lower=[", (eval { pling peen } // "ERR:$@"), "]\n";
  perl: Upper=[pling]  lower=[pling-lc]
  PCL : Upper=[pling]  lower=[ERR:Undefined subroutine &main::peen called ...]

THE SITE, read: `Pl/PExpr.pm` ~line 3017, the general indirect-object
pre-pass --
    if (ref($invocant) eq 'PPI::Token::Word'
        && !$self->is_token_operator($invocant)
        && $invocant->content =~ /^[A-Z]/) {
The all-caps case a few lines below ALREADY has a "known declared package"
exception (`$self->environment->is_package(...)`); the lowercase case has
none, so it never reaches the exception at all.

WHAT MUST BE PROBED BEFORE WIDENING IT (memory: "probe the case it would
BREAK"): `WORD lowercase_bareword` where WORD is a DECLARED sub and the
bareword is NOT a package must keep its current reading.  perl's own
discriminator is #266's callable classifier ("is there a sub of that name in
scope"), and #381 records the twin mis-read in the other direction.  An
emission change: gen bump + the four-population A/B + a full sweep.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md array.t, "126 (`arylen_p`
magic vs `@ISA` element magic)" -- MEASURED WRONG.  The arylen half of the
test (`$#ISA = -1; @ISA = qw(Foo); $ISA[0] = 'Sphare'`) works perfectly in
PCL; only the indirect-object CALL fails, and it fails the same way with no
arylen in sight.

FAMILY: `docs/not-supported.md` "Indirect object syntax with a SCALAR
invocant" (whose text says the CLASS-NAME spellings work -- this narrows that
claim to CAPITALIZED class names); tasks #381, #399.
subject: BUG (indirect object syntax): the general pre-pass requires the invocant bareword to START WITH A CAPITAL, so a method call on a LOWERCASE package name compiles as a sub call -- `pling peen` (with `package peen`) dies "Undefined subroutine &main::peen"
